planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; little pruning is needed beyond shaping right after the spring bloom flush.

directions: Samba is a semi-dwarf selection from the Canadian Dance Series bred at Ottawa, raised from a cross of 'Rumba' and 'Eva Rathke', with coppery bronze new growth that sets off light pink, dark-throated flowers along every branch from late spring into midsummer. The deep green leaves stay edged in purple through the season, and the compact, rounded habit fits small gardens, low informal hedges, and even large containers where full-size weigelas would crowd the space. Grow in full sun for the richest flower and foliage color, and shape lightly right after the main bloom flush since buds form on the previous year's wood.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; prune right after the late-spring bloom since flowers form on old wood.

directions: Czechmark Twopink is a compact weigela bred in the Czech Republic as part of the Czechmark series, smothering its rounded frame in richly saturated pink, trumpet-shaped flowers accented by a darker pink throat for a noticeably two-toned effect each late spring. The bloom is unusually heavy and uniform across the entire plant, giving a solid mound of color rather than scattered flowers. It stays naturally tidy at just over three feet tall and wide, needs no deadheading, and tolerates deer and rabbit browsing better than many weigela cultivars. Prune immediately after flowering to maintain its compact form, since next year's buds set on this season's growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; foliage color develops best with a full day of direct light.

directions: Midnight Sun is grown less for its modest late-spring flush of pink flowers than for foliage that shifts from fresh green in spring to glossy, blazing orange and red tones through summer and into fall, giving the tidy mounded shrub a coleus-like color display without needing yearly replanting. Its diminutive scale, under two feet tall and wide, suits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and large containers where standard weigelas would be oversized. Full sun brings out the most intense foliage color, and the plant resists deer browsing. Shape lightly right after the spring bloom, since next year's flowers set on the current season's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; purple foliage tones intensify with more direct sun exposure.

directions: A newer sport in the My Monet line, this dwarf weigela opens its leaves in cream-and-mint variegation that shifts to soft purple blush where it catches direct sun, then deepens through summer and fall into richer plum and wine-red tones across the whole plant. Small, pink-purple, trumpet-shaped flowers appear in late spring and can repeat sporadically into summer on a compact, rounded frame well under three feet tall. It resists deer browsing and works well in small-space borders, edging, and mixed containers. Trim lightly after the main spring bloom to keep the mound dense, since flower buds set on the previous season's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil; foliage is darkest in full sun and greener in partial shade.

directions: Date Night Tuxedo pairs true white, bell-shaped flowers with foliage so dark it reads almost black in full sun, emerging burgundy in spring before settling into deep green-black for the rest of the season, a striking contrast against the pale blooms from early summer into fall. In partial shade the leaves stay more green, so full sun gives the most dramatic color effect. It reaches a larger, more upright frame than most dwarf weigela selections, making it useful as an accent or informal hedge, and shows good resistance to powdery mildew. Prune to shape immediately after the main flowering period, since next year's buds form on this season's growth.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; gold foliage color is strongest with a full day of direct light.

directions: Found in the Netherlands as a golden-leaved sport of the species selection 'Tor', Glow Girl opens rounded, birch-like leaves in bright yellow that mature to chartreuse through summer before turning red, orange, and purple in fall, giving three seasons of foliage interest on a dense, rounded shrub. Flower buds tinged with red open into flattened white clusters in early summer, a soft complement to the gold foliage rather than the main attraction. It tolerates heat and some drought once established and needs only an occasional light shearing after bloom to stay full and tidy. Full sun brings out the richest leaf color; too much shade causes the gold tones to fade toward plain green.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; shear lightly after bloom to keep the rounded habit tidy.

directions: Wedding Cake improves on the old-fashioned snowmound-type spireas with a denser flower set and a tidier, rounded rather than loosely arching habit, staying under four feet tall and wide. Neat blue-green foliage sets off dense clusters of small, pure white flowers that line the branches in late spring into early summer, and the small serrated leaves turn an attractive coppery bronze in fall. It tolerates average garden soil in full sun to part shade, resists deer and rabbit browsing, and makes a good cut flower. Prune right after flowering if shaping is needed, since bloom forms on the previous year's wood.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; deadhead the first bloom flush to encourage summer rebloom.

directions: Double Play Princess refines the Double Play series with brighter, more saturated pink flower clusters and a more compact, refined habit than earlier series members, blooming in a strong late-spring flush and continuing to repeat through summer on a tidy, low mound. New foliage emerges with reddish tints before settling to green, giving mild seasonal interest beyond the flowers. It is heat- and drought-tolerant once established and needs only an occasional post-bloom shearing to stay dense. Shear off the first round of spent flowers to prompt the characteristic summer rebloom that distinguishes this series from older Japanese spirea cultivars.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter or early spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; prune immediately after flowering since bloom forms on old wood.

directions: Flying Machine stands out among forsythias for flowers noticeably larger than those of standard border types, covering the upright, mounding branches in golden yellow ahead of the foliage each spring. As the blossoms age they twist and spiral as they drop intact, carpeting the ground beneath the shrub in a second, unexpected display. It grows larger than many modern compact forsythia selections, reaching up to eight feet, and tolerates drought and deer browsing better than most flowering shrubs, making it useful for naturalized plantings and informal screens. Rejuvenate older plants every few years by cutting roughly a third of the thickest canes to the ground after bloom, which keeps the shrub flowering heavily on vigorous young wood.
